newsitem.title: USA: Compaq to buy Microcom for $280 million.
newsitem.headline: Compaq to buy Microcom for $280 million.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. said Thursday it has agreed to acquire Microcom Inc., a Norwood, Mass.-based company that makes remote access technologies and computer modems, for $280 million.
Under the deal, Compaq will pay $16.25 for each Microcom share. Microcom stock was up $5.375 to $15.875 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.

"Development of the strategically important and rapidly growing remote access market is a top priority in Compaq's move to expand its communication products business," said Alan Lutz, senior vice president of Compaq's communication products group.
Remote access technologies allow computers users to work on a computer network from another location.

Houston-based Compaq, the world's largest maker of personal computers, said it estimated demand for remote access server computers, that manage will grow from $3 billion in 1996 to $8.3 billion in 2000.
Compaq stock was down $1.50 to $76.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
